text:
nisha: Heads-up: support flagged a surge of 5xx + timeouts from hosted inference in eu-west1 starting ~13:57 UTC. Customers A/B reporting auth failures and long tail token timeouts. Ticket #5241 attached.

alex: seeing the same in metrics — p95 latency up, error rate from gateway -> inference-service. Pulling traces now. :eyes:

jordan: any recent deploys to eu-west1?

deploy-bot: deploy finished: service/inference-gateway @ build-2026.03.11-7c9b38 to eu-west1 at 2026-03-10T13:45:12Z

maria: confirmed a small canary rolled 13:45 UTC (gateway timeout tuning change). Can we rollback?

lee: hold on rollback until we confirm root cause. We saw some auth proxy 502s earlier. That could be cascade.

oncall-aaron: I'll open a war room. Can we get a quick repro for support?

support-bot: customer-reports: 
- customer: acme.ai (prod) 
- symptom: `request times out` or `502` for ~10-40% requests 
- first seen: 2026-03-10T13:57Z 
- sdk: python-sdk v0.9.2

nisha: quick repro I ran: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` sometimes returns `HTTP/1.1 502` or hangs >30s.

alex: paste from gateway logs: 
```
2026-03-10T13:58:03Z ERROR route=generate backend=client-eu-west1 conn=pool-5 msg="upstream timeout" code=504
2026-03-10T13:58:05Z WARN  route=auth proxy=auth-proxy-1 msg="timeout to authz" user=svc-acme
```

jordan: looks like auth-proxy timeouts then upstream yields 504/502. Could be increased latencies in KMS or internal token store. Any KMS alerts?

maria: KMS metrics normal. But there was a short spike of 429s from billing API at 13:57:30Z. Not sure if related.

lee: two hypotheses: 1) gateway timeout tuning + auth proxy spikes -> cascade 2) sudden increase in large-batch generation requests saturating the runtime and causing KV cache stall. Need quick triage steps.

oncall-aaron: Triage plan:
1) throttle new incoming traffic for affected routes (apply 50% rate-limit)
2) route traffic away from eu-west1 to eu-central1 fallback for new requests
3) enable extended logging for auth-proxy and gateway traces
4) avoid deploy rollback unless confirmed

nisha: doing 1 & 2 now. Applying rate-limit on /v1/generate route.

alex: I pushed route override to send 30% of traffic to eu-central1; we'll shift more if errors persist.

maria: enabling debug logs on auth-proxy. Also increasing auth timeout to 10s as temporary mitigation.

jordan: noticed many requests with long prompt lengths (>8k tokens) queued up — those could increase runtime CPU/GPU memory and stall. Any SLO for max prompt?

nisha: we have prompt enforcement but some customers bypass via older SDK. I'm contacting support to ask customer for example payloads.

support-bot: acme.ai provided sample payloads — large-batch with 6x parallel requests and each prompt ~7k tokens.

lee: ok that explains load. For immediate mitigation, can we enforce a soft reject for prompt token > 4k with 429 + retry-after?

oncall-aaron: approved. Add message and docs. Implement soft reject at gateway level (no runtime change).

alex: implemented gateway-level token-size check and soft 429 for >4k in eu-west1. Pushing to other regions next.

maria: auth-proxy timeout bump reduced auth 502s by ~60% in the last 3m. Error rate down from 18% -> 6% but p95 still elevated.

nisha: traffic shift + throttles reduced customer impact to ~5% error rate. Holding on rollback.

jordan: we should still investigate KV cache saturation and batch scheduling. I'll capture runtime queue lengths and GPU utilization for timeline.

alex: captured metrics: runtime queue length spiked at 13:56:45 UTC from 20 -> 420 requests; GPU utilization peaked and KV cache evictions increased.

lee: action item: add guardrail to reject or queue large-batch parallelism >4 concurrent on hosted by default. Owner: lee. ETA: 3 days.

maria: action item: revert gateway timeout tuning change in next safe window if we can't prove it helps. Owner: maria. ETA: 48h.

jordan: action item: runtime team to add backpressure signal to gateway (X-backpressure header) so gateway can decide before overwhelming runtime. Owner: jordan. ETA: 5 days.

nisha: support follow-up: contact acme.ai with mitigation steps and SDK upgrade path, inform about soft 429 and recommended prompt limits. Owner: nisha. ETA: immediate (email drafted).

oncall-aaron: postmortem notes to record: cascade caused by large prompt/parallel batches + gateway timeout tuning + transient billing API 429s causing auth latency spike. Immediate mitigations: route shift, throttles, soft 429, auth timeout bump.

maria: will draft the postmortem and list customer impact windows.

support-bot: customer update sent to acme.ai T=2026-03-10T14:12:05Z — they acknowledged reduced failures but requested root cause and permanent fix timeline.

alex: summary of short-term config changes committed: `gateway: token_size_soft_reject`, `auth-proxy: timeout=10s`, `route_overrides: eu-west1->eu-central1 30%`, `rate_limit: /v1/generate 50%`

jordan: log extracts, metrics, and timeline saved to incident S3: s3://incidents/3141592653/evidence.zip

lee: will schedule a follow-up with runtime to scope longer-term scheduling/backpressure work.

nisha: thanks team. I'll keep this channel updated with the postmortem draft and customer comms. :thumbsup:

maria: closing war room in 20m unless anything new pops up.

oncall-aaron: closing checks: last 10m errors down to baseline 1.2%, p95 trending down. Marking incident as mitigated.

maria: ACTIONS (short list):
- lee: guardrail for parallelism, ETA 3d
- jordan: backpressure header, ETA 5d
- maria: decide on gateway revert or tune, ETA 48h
- nisha: customer comms and SDK guidance, ETA immediate
- alex: follow-up metric dashboard and alerts, ETA 24h

nisha: adding those to the incident tracker now.

support-bot: incident update: mitigated at 2026-03-10T14:18:08Z

alex: good job everyone.
